author: BBC News
description:
UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced a multi-billion pound investment in the armed forces, which he described as the country's "biggest sustained increase" in defence spending since the 1980s. The new expenditure is intended to prepare the British army, navy and air force for the future of war, with an emphasis on drones, AI and autonomous systems.

This comes amid international warnings that Russia could directly threaten Nato countries within the next five years. Britain and its European allies have been ramping up their military spending - spurred by the war in Ukraine and threats by President Donald Trump to withdraw from Nato. 

We ask the BBC's diplomatic correspondent Paul Adams how Nato members are preparing for the future of war, and threats in Europe, the Pacific and beyond.

title: Drone footage shows continued rescue efforts in Venezuela after earthquakes. #Venezuela #BBCNews

author: BBC News
description:
Many areas of Venezuela devastated by last week's twin earthquakes have yet to receive significant government help, leaving residents to carry out much of the rescue effort.
 
In the port of La Guaira, one of the hardest-hit cities, the BBC saw people using crowbars, mallets and pickaxes to try to dig out loved ones and neighbours. Tens of thousands of people are still believed to be missing.
 
More than 1,700 people have been killed in what Interim President Delcy Rodríguez said was the "most brutal natural catastrophe" in Venezuela's history.
 
The BBC's International Correspondent Yogita Limaye reports from the country.

author: BBC News
description:
Police officers have been deployed across South Africa because of fears that anti-immigration protests could turn violent as President Cyril Ramaphosa urged those planning to take part to do so without "intimidation, threats or ultimatums".
 
The planned protests mark an unofficial deadline set by campaigners for all undocumented foreigners to leave the country.
 
Many have already fled to escape violence and intimidation. South African police said 25,000 have been repatriated so far. Most are from other African countries.

author: BBC News
description:
Former Made in Chelsea star and maternity campaigner Louise Thompson quizzed the UK health secretary on a newly announced maternity commissioner role.
 
Thompson said she was "infantalised' during a traumatic labour.
 
James Murray said he will set out the scope for the role "in the next few weeks" before getting it into legislation "as quickly as possible". 
 
It comes after a government-commissioned review found the NHS maternity care system in England is "not fit for the now and not fit for the future".
